name: Founders' Verandah
tagline: Where Technopark's early-stage founders swap honest numbers.
about:
Founders' Verandah began in 2023 on an actual verandah: the front porch of an old Kazhakkoottam house that one of us rented as an office because it was cheaper than a cowork. Eight people building companies around Technopark sat there on a Thursday night with black tea and banana chips and agreed on one rule. Say the real numbers: revenue, runway, churn, the month you couldn't pay yourself.

We're now about ninety founders and would-be founders: SaaS teams selling to the Gulf, a seaweed-snack brand from Vizhinjam, an ed-tech company run by two former teachers, hardware people, and services firms trying to become product firms. Most haven't raised a Series A. Some haven't quit their jobs yet, and they're the people we most want in the room.

Every month there's a Verandah Night, where two founders tell the story of one hard decision and everyone else asks questions. We also run office hours with operators who've done it before, a founder-only peer circle, and a yearly pitch practice day where the investors in the room are told to be kind first and honest second.

No pitching at Verandah Nights, no recruiting at the door, and what's said on the verandah stays there unless the founder says otherwise.

events.name: Verandah Night #31: The Month We Couldn't Make Payroll
events.about:
Two founders, one hard month each. Sreekanth ran out of money in March last year with eleven people on payroll and a cold-chain business that was two weeks from its next contract. Neethu paid salaries late twice in her school-software company's first year. Both told us exactly what happened: the numbers, the conversations with the team, the calls to family, and what they'd do differently.

The room asked questions for an hour. Nobody pitched, nobody took notes on their phones, and at least three people stayed back to talk to Sreekanth about their own runway. This was one of our most attended nights, and one of the quietest.
events.guidelines: Verandah Nights are off the record unless a speaker says otherwise: no recording, no quoting names in posts. No pitching and no recruiting. Doors at 6:45, chai and snacks provided. If it's your first time, tell Lekshmi at the door and she'll introduce you around.

events.name: Pitch Practice Day 2026
events.about:
A full day for founders to pitch, get torn apart gently, fix the pitch and do it again. Each of the twelve presenting founders gave their pitch twice: once in the morning, and once in the afternoon after an hour of one-on-one work with a mentor. The investors in the room had one instruction: kind first, honest second, and always say the one thing that would make you take a second meeting.

The other founders in the room weren't spectators. Everyone scored every pitch on a simple sheet, and the scores were compared with the investors' at the end. The gap between what founders thought mattered and what the investors actually noticed was the most useful slide of the day.
events.guidelines: Presenting founders: seven minutes, ten slides at most, no videos. Send your deck by Thursday night. Non-presenting founders: you're a scorer, so come ready to pay attention. The fee covers lunch, tea and the printed scoring kits. Decks are shared only with the panel and deleted after the event.

events.name: Selling SaaS to the Gulf: A Field Guide
events.about:
Half the SaaS founders in our community sell, or want to sell, to customers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Oman. Shalini has sold clinic software there for six years, and Firoz has had about six hundred procurement conversations with Gulf hospitals and clinics from his desk in Dubai. Together they walked through what actually works.

Topics included: why your first customer will probably come through a Malayali relative of someone you know, pricing in dirhams versus dollars, Arabic in the interface, the procurement calendar around Ramadan, and why a trip to Dubai in month three is worth more than six months of cold email.
events.guidelines: Online, on a video call; the link arrives an hour before. Cameras optional. Questions go in the chat and the hosts will pick them up in the last thirty minutes. The session is recorded for members who couldn't attend.

events.name: Verandah Night #34: Letting Go of Your First Hire
events.about:
The first person you hire is often a friend, a cousin or the first person who believed in you. Letting them go is one of the hardest things a founder does, and almost nobody talks about it. This month, Prasanth tells the story of the six people he has had to let go and why he waited too long with the first one.

Dr. Sheeba Alexander, who advises founders on difficult conversations, will join him to talk about how to do it with dignity: what to say, what never to say, and how to look after the team who stays. As always, the questions afterwards are the main event.
events.guidelines: Off the record, as every Verandah Night is. Please don't share names or details from the talk. No pitching, no recruiting. Doors at 6:45; chai and snacks provided. First-timers, say hello to Lekshmi at the door.

speakers.bio: Has hired forty people and let go of six, and says the first one should have happened a year earlier than it did.

speakers.bio: Advises founders on hard conversations and keeps a list of sentences you should never say in one.

events.name: Founders' Dinner: The Bootstrapped Edition
events.about:
Thirty founders, one long table in the courtyard, and a Kerala dinner cooked by the family who own the building. This edition is for founders who haven't raised money and don't plan to: people building profitable companies on revenue alone. Our guest, Unnikrishnan, has run an unfunded accounting software company from Kazhakkoottam for eleven years.

There are no talks. Every few courses, the seating changes so you sit next to someone new. Lekshmi will hand each table one question to start with, and after that the conversation is yours.
events.guidelines: This dinner is full; join the waitlist on the event page if you'd like a seat at the next one. Please tell us about food allergies in your registration. The fee covers the dinner and is shared with the family who cooks it. Arrive by 7:15 so seating can start on time.
